AUCTION COMMANDS

One authoritative signal at a time.

narrative.overview: Code Premier League uses the visual logic of a live production switcher: dense but ordered channels, obvious tally states, hard-working labels, and one dominant signal at a time. Light paper surfaces introduce and onboard; deep ink surfaces take over once play begins.
keyCharacteristics: Condensed, uppercase display typography for commands and live state.
Matte ink panels divided by fine structural channels.
Coral for actions, lime for live state, cyan for identity, and gold for time.
Initials-based player geometry instead of photographic likenesses.
Compact mobile reflow that preserves the auction decision surface.

rules.name: The Signal Has Meaning Rule
rules.body: Coral means act, lime means live or leading, cyan means identify, and gold means time.

rules.name: The Numeral Leads Rule
rules.body: Auction time, bid value, room code, and final score always outrank their labels in size and contrast.

rules.name: The Console Stays Flat Rule
rules.body: Dark live-play panels do not use soft card shadows; border channels and tonal layers define hierarchy.

dos: Do give one live number clear visual authority on every auction surface.
Do preserve 44px minimum controls and the stacked mobile auction layout.
Do label every automated mode and simulated rating plainly.
Do use hairline channels to make dense information scannable.
Do keep score weights, penalties, and budget effects visible and explainable.
donts: Don't replace the control-room grammar with generic rounded dashboard cards.
Don't use glow, glass, gradient text, or decorative neon as shorthand for gaming.
Don't use signal colors without their established semantic role.
Don't introduce real league marks, athlete likenesses, money imagery, or betting language.
Don't hide the active bid, countdown, budget, or final score behind hover-only interaction.
